2.0 removes the include loader. SMK does not use it, and a Host loads its plugin scripts itself and registers them on SMK.TYPE. host-contract.test.ts holds this.
v2 publishes SMK.SUPPORT, the support manifest the build reads off the file tree. 1.0 had no equivalent. Added, not lost.
v2 registers maplibre, and registers esri3d at load where 1.0 resolved it lazily through AMD. onlyAdded means a viewer that leaves the 1.0 side is never covered.
v2 registers each tool class on SMK.TYPE; 1.0 kept them inside its AMD modules. onlyAdded means a name that leaves the 1.0 side is never covered by this ruling.
The whole point of axis B: the candidate is a different viewer, so this field must differ.

Measured again 2026-09-07 with both panes the same box: the zoom is EQUAL. The earlier 'zoom 5 against zoom 4' was the harness, not SMK - the 1.0 page gave the map the whole window and the v2 pane frame is 480px tall. What is left is a centre about 2 pixels apart at the opening scale, which is rounding in the fit. axis-a.test.ts asserts the zoom on its own, so a real change still fails.

MapLibre counts zoom for 512px tiles and Leaflet for 256, and Leaflet's zoomSnap rounds a fit to a whole level. One viewer.location.zoom in a Config means two scales. Normalising it moves every Host config and every saved bookmark, so it needs a ruling, not a patch - CONTEXT.md 8.1.

A viewer modifier beside the neutral class. Both viewers now render smk-minimap, which is what a Theme selects on; smk-minimap-leaflet and smk-minimap-maplibre are extras for anything that must tell them apart. D9: converge on viewer-neutral, keep the modifier.

mode is a MapLibre-only tool - the support manifest says so. In Leaflet the shared half still builds, so the tool exists and is disabled and not visible. That is the documented no-viewer-half case, not a fault. See CONTEXT.md 8.2.

The class component.ts puts on a tool whose visible flag is true. It is here because mode is visible in MapLibre and does not exist in Leaflet - see the ModeTool toolState ruling. Not a chrome difference of its own.

The default Basemap - decision D11, 2026-09-08. SMK 1.0 opens on the Esri Topographic basemap, whose id is deprecated in v2 and hidden by the picker. v2 opens on bc-roads, the GeoBC BC Basemap service. Since D17 it draws with the style GeoBC published on its ArcGIS item, which adds a hillshade - see the item and hillshade rulings. The candidate fetches the service description, the glyphs and the tiles - all of it this one decision.

Decision D17, 2026-09-17. bc-roads draws BC Basemap as GeoBC designed and published it: the style, sprite and item description of the ArcGIS item for the standard version, with hillshade. SMK 1.0 opened on Esri Topographic and asked none of it.
Decision D17, 2026-09-17. The second source of GeoBC's published BC Basemap style. Its layers draw from zoom 4 to 12. SMK 1.0 had no hillshade.
The 1.0 side of the default basemap decision. See the BC_BASEMAP_20240307 ruling and D11.

The default BC basemap through two client libraries. esri-leaflet-vector reads the VectorTileServer description first; MapLibre goes straight to resources/styles/root.json and takes the tile template from there. Both draw the same map. D9 wire behaviour: each Viewer uses its own native call.

The D17 item through two client libraries. esri-leaflet-vector reads the item description and moves the sprite to cdn.arcgis.com; MapLibre reads the item style from the CDN and takes the sprite from www.arcgis.com, where the style points. Same files, same map. D9 wire behaviour.

The D17 hillshade source. esri-leaflet-vector keeps the source url, so MapLibre inside it reads the service description as TileJSON; the MapLibre viewer uses the tile template the style gives. Both fetch the same hillshade tiles - 8 each at zoom 6 over the Coast Mountains, measured 2026-09-17. D9 wire behaviour.

esri-dynamic. Both viewers now call /export - that was the 2026-09-07 fix. esri-leaflet asks for JSON and then fetches the image the service produced under arcgisoutput/; MapLibre uses the export url straight as a raster tile template. Same endpoint, two client strategies. Leaflet also sends dpi=96, which is the service default.
The Leaflet side of the same esri-dynamic export. See the _ags_map ruling.
esri-leaflet reads the service description before it exports. See the _ags_map ruling.
esri-leaflet's own notice that L.esri.BasemapLayer is in mature support. SMK 1.0 opens on that basemap; v2 opens on the Canada Topography composite and never builds one.
Registration order, the same notice as on axis A. It reaches both viewers, so it only shows here when one pane starts a tool the other does not.

esri-feature. Both viewers fetch the features now - that was the 2026-09-07 fix; before it, the Leaflet layer threw at creation and never drew. esri-leaflet tiles its feature queries, so it sends eight /query calls with resultType=tile; MapLibre fetches once with where=1=1. Same service, two client strategies. D9 wire behaviour.

esri-dynamic. v2 exports the map; SMK 1.0 asked the service for nothing at all, because it built a featureLayer against the MapServer root and that request never produced a drawing. Fixed on 2026-09-07 - v2 does more than 1.0 here, not less. D9 wire behaviour.
The export call itself. See the bcgw_MapServer ruling.

dist/smk.es.js calls require() for the ESRI 3D viewer modules at load, whichever viewer runs. A host page that does not load the ArcGIS API - as one that never wanted the 3D viewer would not - gets this once. Measured 2026-09-07 and recorded in CONTEXT.md 8.1; the host-contract test guards it so it cannot grow.

The Leaflet minimap keeps smk-spacer beside the neutral smk-minimap, because SMK 1.0 rendered it and a class a Host can see is a contract (D9). MapLibre never had one. The neutral class is what a Theme selects on.
The basemap status class carries the basemap id, and the default changed by decision - Topographic in 1.0, topographic-v2 in v2. See D22.
Added. Both viewer halves now render a neutral smk-minimap so a Theme need not know which Viewer is running; 1.0 had only the spacer, which v2 still renders too.
SMK 1.0 itself throws this when the whole catalogue is built - it is the REFERENCE side, so it says nothing about the rewrite. Recorded so it cannot be mistaken for a v2 fault.

SETTLED 2026-09-08 by driving the panel's real commands. v2 renders the layers panel and fetches its legends when the panel OPENS; SMK 1.0 did both at start. Both end with four getlegendgraphic requests and four legend rows, in both 2D Viewers - legend.test.ts holds it. Lazier, not lost. The one visible consequence: a Host that reads the DOM for legend rows before anything is opened finds none.

SETTLED 2026-09-08. smk-obscured sits on a layer display row, which renders with the rest of the layers panel - at start in SMK 1.0, on open in v2. Same cause as the smk-legend ruling, and the class still renders when a layer is not actually visible.
The v2 side of the same layers-panel difference. The class exists in 1.0 too.

v2 declares a customLabel prop in the tool-panel-feature component that one tool does not have. Its own notice, on the candidate side, and harmless - but worth tidying.
The tool reports the basemap it is on, and the default changed by decision - Topographic in 1.0, topographic-v2 in v2. See D22.
